sourceKind: user-supplied real-world reference photographs (three, not AI-generated)
scopeNote: This is the v1 open-frame-cart shape's reference set only. It predates and is separate from the v2 throne-cart rebuild's own reference (a later AI-generated concept sheet, see object-sculpt-spec.json's authoringNote/sourceImage). Only a few v1 measurements (RICKSHAW_SCALE, the wheel hub/spoke fix, the shaft cross-brace position) carry forward into v2 unchanged; the throne, cushion, lantern, and banner design in v2 comes from the concept sheet, not these photographs.
permissionContext: The user supplied three real photographs of hand-pulled rickshaws in conversation and asked for a new game mount inspired by their shape, to be built as a Halloween/skeleton-puller theme.
shippingPolicy: None of the three source images or derived crops are committed or shipped. Only silhouette, proportion, and construction-logic observations are carried into the v1 sculpt spec and factory code.

sources.description: Color photo, classic Kolkata-style hand-pulled rickshaw, canopy raised, parked against a barred window and wall covered in unrelated tutoring-service posters.
Black-and-white photo, same rickshaw style, canopy fully collapsed, no cover fabric visible at all: shows the bare rib/frame structure and rear cross-bracing with nothing occluding it.

Color photo, modern manufactured reproduction rickshaw (commercial product photo, carries a visible manufacturer watermark/logo in-frame), canopy raised, cleaner tubular-steel construction and a distinct rear profile with flared mudguard-style wheel arches.
sources.role: secondary construction reference (rear three-quarter, canopy support geometry)

kept: two-wheel hand-pulled cart silhouette: large wire-spoke wheels flanking a low bench seat
sloped footboard/step at the front of the seat, ahead of the wheels
two long, roughly parallel forward-reaching shafts (the puller's handles), meeting the cart body near the wheel axle line
wheel hub and spoke rhythm (evenly spaced thin spokes, a visibly thicker rim)
excluded: the modern-repro photo's manufacturer watermark/logo and any brand identity
the extended-canopy photo's background: barred window, wall, and unrelated posters
any real-world manufacturer name, decal, or plate
the specific upholstery colors (dark green bench, black lacquer body) as a literal palette to copy exactly
exact heraldry or paint scheme from either photographed unit

the folding canopy both photographed units show: cut from v1 for real crown-clearance and unsupported-spoke problems and never shipped in any pass, including v2 (see object-sculpt-spec.json's omitOrSimplify)
originalTreatment: the integrated skeleton-torso puller: arms/hands pinned to the shaft handles, composed as a separate runtime actor rather than baked into this mesh, no photo shows this, fully invented
a Halloween-appropriate material palette: weathered bone, aged dark iron, rather than the photographed gloss-black lacquer and clean upholstery
project-authored rear and underside geometry (none of the three photos show a clean rear three-quarter; the modern-repro photo's rear view informs proportions only, not exact form)

front-three-quarter.description: Front-left three-quarter view of the classic rickshaw, canopy raised, showing wheel spoke rhythm, footboard slope, shaft angle, and canopy rib fan.

frame-detail.description: Side-on view of the bare frame with canopy collapsed: rear cross-bracing, seat-back structure, and how the canopy ribs fold down when not in use.

rear-three-quarter.description: Rear-left three-quarter view of the modern reproduction, canopy raised: informs the rear seat-back curve, canopy support strut angle, and wheel arch relationship not visible in the other two references.
